investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled, and no agent VM identity or state is ever returned to the eval runner. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing running agents or leaked/stuck pods that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] A node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes that does not include the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, or the affinity rules have drifted such that only 4 ineligible nodes are selected, effectively reducing usable capacity to zero.
[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are under memory or CPU pressure in addition to the VM resource exhaustion, preventing preemption of any existing workloads.
[Possible] A prior eval run or production workload left orphaned remote-agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (resource leak).

[Lower likelihood] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quantity advertised by the node kubelet was reduced (e.g., by a node configuration change or device plugin restart) without a corresponding reduction in scheduled workloads, creating an over-committed state.

If no orphaned remote-agent pods are found on the cluster, a resource leak is not contributing to the exhaustion, and the capacity limit itself is simply too low for the current workload.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Blocks All Remote Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T21:22–21:27Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements for remote agent workloads. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod timed out (145 s for remote-agent-state, 124 s for remote-agent-create, 145 s for remote-agent-runtime), preventing the eval runner from reaching the state-polling stage and producing any evidence. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes: concurrent workloads or a previous eval run consumed all available VM slots and they were not released before this eval window, leaving 0/6 nodes schedulable.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only the 2 peer-pod nodes carry; if those 2 nodes are at capacity there is no fallback, making the cluster effectively zero-capacity for this workload type.

Tertiary — a leaked or stuck remote agent pod from a prior eval run (e.g., a cleanup failure in withCleanup) holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on one or both peer-pod nodes, preventing new pods from being scheduled.
Quaternary — cluster autoscaler not configured or not triggered for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes, so capacity was not expanded to meet demand during the eval window.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never provisioned, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector, leaving 0 of 6 nodes available for scheduling. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled, and no agent VM identity or state is ever returned to the eval runner. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] The kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing running agents or leaked/stuck pods that were not cleaned up, leaving no capacity for new pods.

[Likely] A node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes that does not include the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes, or the affinity rules have drifted such that only 4 ineligible nodes are selected, effectively reducing usable capacity to zero.
[Possible] The 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes are under memory or CPU pressure in addition to the VM resource exhaustion, preventing preemption of any existing workloads.
[Possible] A prior eval run or production workload left orphaned remote-agent pods running on the 2 eligible nodes, consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them (resource leak).

[Lower likelihood] The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quantity advertised by the node kubelet was reduced (e.g., by a node configuration change or device plugin restart) without a corresponding reduction in scheduled workloads, creating an over-committed state.

Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to fail completely.

With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every attempt to provision a remote agent pod timed out (145 s for remote-agent-state, 124 s for remote-agent-create, 145 s for remote-agent-runtime), preventing the eval runner from reaching the state-polling stage and producing any evidence. Add a cluster node availability eval that asserts at least one node matches the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector and has non-zero kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, running on a shorter interval than the remote-agent checks.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold (e.g., 10 minutes) and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Refine the remote-agent-state eval to distinguish between a scheduling failure (pod never created) and a state-polling failure (pod created but state not returned), so the failure message and evidence gap are more precisely localized.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Nodes Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-27T21:24–21:27Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes swarm cluster was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource were fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No agent pod reached a running state, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent provisioning has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the agent pod: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (the resource quota on those nodes was already consumed), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption could not help because no lower-priority victims existed on the 2 eligible nodes and preemption is not applicable on the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained Unschedulable for 145 seconds before the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing every contract assertion. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which must schedule a pod before any evidence can be collected.
source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270: contract at line 268 requires orgId, agentId, model, provider, message — none present because pod scheduling failed upstream.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent agent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots consumed, leaving no capacity for the eval pod. Supported directly by failed-check.message and both sibling check messages.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were correctly sized but the affinity rules are too restrictive, capacity appears lower than the physical cluster total.

TERTIARY — Cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across all eligible nodes is too small to absorb concurrent eval and production workloads simultaneously, causing contention during the eval window.

QUATERNARY — Stale or leaked VM allocations: a previous agent pod that was not cleaned up may be holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, preventing new scheduling. The runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs line 1916) but a prior failed cleanup could leave a slot occupied.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity on the 2 eligible cluster nodes immediately to determine current allocatable vs. consumed slots.

Audit all pods currently requesting kata.peerpods.io/vm across all namespaces to identify any leaked or long-running pods that should have been cleaned up by the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs.

Review the node affinity/selector rules in the remote agent pod spec against the labels on all 6 cluster nodes to determine whether the 4 non-matching nodes can be made eligible, increasing the effective scheduling pool.

If resource exhaustion is confirmed, evaluate whether the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota on the 2 eligible nodes can be increased or whether additional nodes with this resource can be added to the cluster.

Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any remediation to confirm recovery and collect the required evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) against the contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 266-270.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe node on the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes shows available (unallocated) VM slots at the time of the eval run, the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler bug or pod spec error.
If the remote-agent-create check passes on a subsequent run without any cluster changes, it would suggest a transient contention spike rather than a sustained capacity deficit.

If the 4 affinity-mismatched nodes are found to carry kata.peerpods.io/vm resources but were excluded due to a pod spec label error, the root cause would be a misconfigured node selector rather than resource exhaustion.

If a passing run of local-agent-create or local-agent-runtime is observed at the same timestamp, it would confirm the failure is isolated to the remote (kata.peerpods.io/vm) scheduling path and not a broader cluster or API outage.
If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of failure, the cause would shift to a quota configuration error (allocatable set to 0) rather than runtime exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity across all cluster nodes before attempting agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct check rather than a scheduling timeout.
Add a node-affinity-coverage eval that verifies at least N nodes satisfy the remote agent pod's affinity/selector rules, alerting before capacity drops to a critically small pool.
Add a pod-cleanup verification eval that confirms no orphaned remote agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots remain after each eval run, catching withCleanup failures early.
Add a concurrent-scheduling eval that attempts to create two remote agent pods simultaneously to measure true available parallelism and detect contention before it causes eval timeouts.
Consider a latency-banded eval that warns at the warningLatencyMs threshold (300000 ms) before the full outageLatencyMs (420000 ms) is reached, giving earlier signal of scheduling slowdowns.
